provenance: Two device sources, both captured — no row is hand-written. (1) CHR 7.23.3 x86: :put [:parse "<input>"] round-tripped via bun run .scratch/explain-parse-oracle.ts and the cliref sweep; 7.24rc2 showed the same forms. Every row whose `input` is a literal CLI string comes from here. (2) lsp-routeros-ts corpus IL oracle (test-data/corpus.sqlite, parseil_results.il_text), RouterOS 7.20.8 / 7.22.1 / 7.23rc1 — whole-file :parse of real-world scripts. Rows carrying `corpusScript` are verbatim il_text fragments from there and are marked as such; their `input` names the corpus path, not a CLI string. The wrapper that only watches for a thrown error records parse-ok for every input (GH#230 control). Read the return value's text instead — it is a diagnostic value, not a throw.
notes: The oracle is the PRINTED VALUE of :parse, not a throw. Console (mac-telnet/ssh) prints it; REST (HTTP 200 ret) and native API (as-string ret) return the same text.
Fixtures are 7.23.3 (stable) x86. Pin 7.23.3 wording; tolerate form drift across 7.24rc2 only where called out.
`bad parameter` is a NAME-level verdict only — it does not check value types (/ip/address/add address=not-an-ip still passes). `}`/`)/bad values were accepted in the sweep (see GH#230 reach limits).
`column` is RouterOS's 1-based byte offset; the issue requires a column→byte mapping and its UTF-8 failure mode before any byte span.
`/ip addr print` canonicalizes to `/ip/address/print` inside the returned value — the canonicalization is per-input, not per-path-table.

Each classification entry carries `raw`: the exact printed `:parse` value as captured on a device — CHR 7.23.3 for CLI-string rows, corpus il_text for `corpusScript` rows. Tests classify `raw`, not the `expectedContains` fragment. Never hand-write a `raw`.

For script-shaped input the accepted return echoes the statement body, so RouterOS's own IL spelling matters: statement heads print with a LEADING SLASH (`(evl /globalname=…)`, `(evl /putmessage=…)`), never `(evl :globalname=…)`; a `where` clause prints as `…/findwhere=$field;$field;…` with `$`-prefixed names. Zero corpus rows use the `(evl :` form.

Because the body is echoed, the word `expected` in source text is not a rejection (GH#230 blocker, ~1.3% FP on the corpus before the fix). Only `expected … (line N column M)` / `syntax error … (line N column M)`, or the `(<%%` menu wrapper, is a reject.
Corpus-verified against all 2736 parseil_results rows with the shipped classifyParseResult: 0 false positives, 0 false negatives.
